claims.text: A single-source mixture of at least five noble-metal precursors can be used to target single-phase high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Rapid heating and cooling restrict precursor or atomic mobility during decomposition.
Formation of single-phase noble-metal HEA nanoparticles is governed by stochastic principles and inhibition of precursor mobility.
Limited atomic mobility restricts long-range diffusion during rapid thermal cycling.
Restricted mobility forces stochastic incorporation before the elements can segregate.
Stochastic incorporation locks in a metastable single-phase solid solution.
Extending the thermal hold or slowing cooling increases atomic diffusion and precursor mobility.
Greater mobility allows differences in reduction kinetics and local driving forces to cause elemental segregation.
Greater mobility promotes phase separation and mixed or multiphase structures.
Low-mobility rapid-heating and rapid-cooling conditions consistently produce a uniform single-phase crystal structure.
Low-mobility processing produces controlled nanoparticle morphology.
Low-mobility processing produces lower observed decomposition temperatures.
Increasing precursor mobility produces more irregular nanoparticle morphologies.
Increasing precursor mobility raises the effective thermal decomposition temperature.
The rapid-heating and rapid-cooling baseline tends toward a predominantly single-phase state, although slight inhomogeneities may occur.
The proposed mechanism applies specifically to noble-metal HEAs containing more than five elements.
The mobility effect is most pronounced when constituent elements have diverse reduction rates.
Significant differences in atomic sizes define an applicable boundary for the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial-state and conditions fields include systems with exactly five elements ('five or more' and 'at least five'), whereas the boundary field restricts applicability to systems with more than five elements.

The predicted outcome says low-mobility rapid processing will consistently yield a uniform single phase, while the stated rapid-cycle baseline allows slight inhomogeneities and only a predominantly single-phase state.
